Maintenance Report — MNT-0108-004

Asset: WELL-0108 (NE-07 Well 108, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 14 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Apr 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0108-0026 on 2023-04-13 Report written: 14 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0108-0026 at 13:15 on 2023-04-13 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.4% of the pad area, estimated 4.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 346 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 277 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0108-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.45% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0108-026

Asset: WELL-0108 (NE-07 Well 108, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 26 May 2026 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 941 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0108-0180 on 2026-04-16 Report written: 26 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0108-0180 showed the wellhead at 20.4 °C with the air at 20.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
